overview: A one-page list of papers for State Department file 894.6355, concerning zinc mining in Japan. It indexes a document reporting the Nippon Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha’s unsuccessful attempt to acquire Japanese rights to a zinc-smelting process controlled by the New Jersey Zinc Company, with copies of the relevant correspondence enclosed.

subfiles.title: List of papers: Zinc mining in Japan
subfiles.about: The sheet indexes correspondence concerning an unsuccessful Japanese effort to obtain rights to a New Jersey Zinc Company smelting process.
subfiles.summary: This filing sheet identifies the subject as zinc mining in Japan and lists one paper dated January 18. According to its précis, the paper enclosed copies of correspondence documenting Nippon Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha’s unsuccessful attempt to secure Japanese rights to a zinc-smelting process controlled by the New Jersey Zinc Company.

interest: The sheet is useful as evidence of attempted industrial technology transfer between an American zinc company and a major Japanese mining enterprise. Although the underlying correspondence is not reproduced here, the précis records both the commercial objective and its failure, making the page a concise lead for research into patents, metallurgy, and U.S.–Japanese industrial relations.
